# 3-Month Home Maintenance Plan for a Houston 2-Story House

A focused 90-day plan for an 18-year-old home in Houston, with priorities on **safety, energy efficiency, and preventing emergencies**. Budget is set to **USD 1,200**, so this plan concentrates on the highest-risk systems first: HVAC, roof/drainage, electrical/safety devices, plumbing, and garage access.

## Priority Maintenance Roadmap

| Month | Goal | Key Tasks | Est. Cost |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Month 1 | Reduce emergency risk | HVAC tune-up; replace filters; test smoke/CO alarms; inspect attic, roof edges, and gutters; check garage door safety reversal | USD 350–500 |
| Month 2 | Improve efficiency | Seal air leaks; add weatherstripping; insulate exposed HVAC lines; clean outdoor condenser area; flush water heater if accessible | USD 200–350 |
| Month 3 | Catch hidden issues | Plumbing leak check; electrical outlet/GFCI test; inspect caulk around windows/doors; service garage opener; review pest/moisture signs | USD 250–400 |

## 90-Day Home Maintenance Plan

### Month 1: Safety and system health first
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

- **HVAC**
  - Hire out a full HVAC inspection and tune-up for the central system.
  - Replace filters immediately and set a recurring 30–60 day schedule.
  - Check condensate drain, thermostat accuracy, and refrigerant performance.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 120–220

- **Life safety**
  - Test smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms.
  - Replace batteries and any unit older than 10 years.
  - Add alarms if coverage is incomplete on each level and near sleeping areas.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 40–180

- **Roof, gutters, and drainage**
  - Inspect roof shingles, flashing, and visible attic signs of leaks.
  - Clean gutters/downspouts and confirm water moves away from the foundation.
  - In Houston, this is especially important before heavy rain and storm season.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 0–150 if DIY; USD 100–200 if hired out

- **Garage safety**
  - Test automatic reversal on the garage door.
  - Inspect springs, tracks, rollers, and opener function.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 0–125 DIY; USD 125–250 professional service

### Month 2: Energy efficiency and moisture control
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/wind.svg

- **Air sealing**
  - Seal gaps around doors, attic penetrations, plumbing penetrations, and visible wall openings.
  - Add weatherstripping where air leaks are obvious.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 40–120 DIY; USD 150–300 hired out

- **HVAC efficiency**
  - Clean debris around the outdoor condenser and maintain 2 feet of clearance.
  - Inspect attic ductwork for disconnected joints or damaged insulation.
  - Insulate accessible refrigerant lines if missing or deteriorated.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 30–100 DIY; USD 150–300 if duct repairs are needed

- **Water heater**
  - Flush sediment if the tank is accessible and in good condition.
  - Check for corrosion, leaks, and temperature setting.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 0–40 DIY; USD 100–180 professional flush/service

- **Windows and doors**
  - Re-caulk cracked exterior joints and seal obvious drafts.
  - Focus on sun-exposed and rain-exposed sides first.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 25–100 DIY; USD 150–250 hired out

### Month 3: Hidden defects and emergency prevention
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shield-check.svg

- **Plumbing**
  - Check under sinks, around toilets, at water heater connections, and in the laundry area.
  - Look for slow leaks, staining, soft flooring, and mold odors.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 0 DIY inspection; USD 125–300 if repairs are needed

- **Electrical**
  - Test GFCI outlets in kitchens, baths, garage, and exterior locations.
  - Check for warm outlets, flickering lights, or tripped breakers.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 0–60 DIY; USD 150–350 electrician if issues are found

- **Pest and moisture prevention**
  - Inspect attic, garage, and perimeter for pest entry points and moisture intrusion.
  - Seal small gaps and keep stored items off garage floors and attic decking.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 20–80 DIY; USD 150–400 pest control if active infestation exists

- **Final review**
  - Revisit the HVAC filter, drain lines, and thermostat settings.
  - Create a simple maintenance log with dates and service notes.
  - **Estimated cost:** USD 0–25

## What to Do Yourself vs Hire Out

| Task | Homeowner Can Do | Hire Out When |
|---|---|---|
| Replace HVAC filters | Yes | If access is difficult or system needs repeated clogging diagnosis |
| Test alarms and GFCIs | Yes | If any device fails or wiring seems unsafe |
| Clean gutters | Yes if safely reachable | If roof pitch, height, or ladder risk is high |
| Caulk/weatherstrip | Yes | If large gaps, rot, or water intrusion is present |
| Inspect for leaks | Yes | If leak source is hidden or damage is spreading |
| Flush water heater | Yes for many tanks | If unit is older, corroded, or has valve issues |
| Garage door adjustment | Basic checks only | For springs, cables, opener logic, or reversal failure |
| HVAC tune-up/repair | No | Yes, especially for refrigerant, electrical, or drainage issues |

## Budget Allocation That Fits USD 1,200

- **HVAC service and filter replacement:** USD 180–260
- **Safety devices and batteries:** USD 40–180
- **Gutters, sealing, caulk, weatherstripping, minor materials:** USD 100–300
- **Plumbing/electrical inspection or minor repairs:** USD 150–350
- **Garage door service:** USD 125–250
- **Contingency for small repairs:** USD 150–250

**Recommended target spend:** about **USD 900–1,100**, leaving a cushion for surprise fixes.

## Seasonal Tasks for Houston

- **Before storm season:** roof, gutters, drainage, tree limbs, window seals
- **Before peak summer heat:** HVAC tune-up, filter change, attic heat checks, condenser clearance
- **During humid months:** moisture, mold, plumbing leaks, bathroom ventilation
- **Before cooler weather:** inspect weatherstripping, alarms, furnace/heat function if applicable

## Quick Actions
